translations.text: Since many have undertaken to draw up an account of the things established among us,
just as those who were eyewitnesses and servants of the word from the beginning handed them down to us,
it also seemed good to me, having [?] everything accurately, to write an orderly account to you, most excellent Theophilus,
so that you may know the certainty of the things you have been taught.
In the days of Herod, king of Judea, there was a priest named Zechariah, from the priestly division of Abijah. His wife was one of Aaron’s descendants, and her name was Elizabeth.
They were both righteous before God, living blamelessly according to all the Lord’s commandments and ordinances.
They had no child, because Elizabeth was barren, and both were advanced in years.
While he was serving as priest before God when his division was on duty,
according to the priestly custom, it fell to him to enter the Lord’s temple and burn incense.
The whole gathering of people was praying outside at the time of the incense offering.
An angel of the Lord appeared to him, standing to the right of the altar of incense.
Zechariah was troubled when he saw him, and fear fell upon him.
But the angel of the Lord said to him, “Do not be afraid, Zechariah, because your prayer has been heard. Your wife Elizabeth will bear you a son, and you shall name him John.
You will have great joy, and many will rejoice at his birth.
For he will be great before God. He will drink neither wine nor strong drink, and he will be filled with the Holy Spirit even from his mother’s womb.
He will turn many of the children of Israel to the Lord their God.
He will go before him in the spirit and power of Elijah, to turn the hearts of fathers to their children, and the disobedient to the wisdom of the righteous, to prepare a perfected people.”
Zechariah said to the angel, “How shall I know this? For I am an old man, and my wife is advanced in years.”
The angel answered him, “I am Gabriel, who stands before God. I was sent to speak to you and bring you this good news.
And now you will be silent and unable to speak until the day these things happen, because you did not believe my words, which will be fulfilled at their proper time.”
The people were waiting for Zechariah and wondering why he was taking so long in the temple.
When he came out, he could not speak to them. They realized that he had seen a vision in the temple. He kept making signs to them and remained unable to speak.
When the days of his service were completed, he went home.
After those days, his wife Elizabeth conceived, and she kept herself hidden for four months, saying,
For the Lord has done this for me in the days when he looked upon me, to take away my disgrace among people.
In the sixth month, the archangel Gabriel was sent by God to a town in Galilee named Nazareth,
to a virgin betrothed to a man named Joseph, of the house of David. The virgin’s name was Mary.
And the angel came in to her and said, “Rejoice, favored one! The Lord is with you. Blessed are you among women.”
When she saw him, she was troubled by his words and wondered what kind of greeting this might be.
The angel said to her, “Do not be afraid, Mary, for you have found favor with God.
Look, you will conceive in your womb and bear a son, and you will name him Jesus.
He will be great and will be called the Son of the Most High. The Lord God will give him the throne of his father David,
and he will reign over the house of Jacob forever. His kingdom will have no end.”
Mary said to the angel, “How will this happen, since I have not had relations with a man?”
The angel answered her, “The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you. Therefore the child to be born will be called holy, the Son of God.
And look, Elizabeth your relative has also conceived a son in her old age, and this is the sixth month for her who was called barren.
For no word from God will be powerless.
Then Mary said, “Here I am, the Lord’s servant. Let it happen to me according to your word.” And the angel departed from her.
Mary arose and went in haste into the hill country, to a town in Judah.
She entered Zechariah’s house and greeted Elizabeth.
When Elizabeth heard Mary’s greeting, the child leaped for joy in her womb, and Elizabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit.
She cried out in a loud voice and said, “Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb!
Why has this been granted to me, that the mother of my Lord should come to me?
For as soon as the sound of your greeting reached my ears, the child in my womb leaped for joy.
Blessed is she who believed, for what was spoken to her by the Lord will be fulfilled.”
Mary said, “My soul magnifies the Lord,
and my spirit has rejoiced in God my Savior,
because he has looked upon the lowly state of his servant. For from now on all generations will call me blessed,
because the Mighty One has done great things for me, and holy is his name.”
Mary stayed with her for about three months and returned to her own home.
The time came for Elizabeth to give birth, and she bore a son.
Those living nearby heard of her child's birth and that the Lord had shown her great mercy, and they rejoiced with her.
And on the eighth day they came to circumcise the child, and they were calling him Zechariah after his father.
But his mother answered, “No; his name is to be John.”
They said to her, “There is no one in your family who is called by that name.”
They made signs to his father to find out what he wanted to name him.
And he asked for a writing tablet and wrote, “His name is John.” And they all marveled.
Immediately his mouth and his tongue were opened, and he spoke, praising God.
Fear came upon all those living nearby, and all these things were being discussed throughout the hill country of Judea.
All who heard these things took them to heart, saying, “What, then, will this child become?” And the Lord's hand was with him.
His father Zechariah was filled with the Holy Spirit and prophesied, saying:
“Blessed is the Lord, the God of Israel, for he has visited his people and brought them redemption.
And you, child, will be called a prophet of the Most High, for you will go before the Lord to prepare his paths.”
The child grew and became strong in spirit, and he was in the wilderness until the day of his public appearance to Israel.
A decree went out from Caesar Augustus that the whole inhabited world should be registered.
This was the first registration, when Quirinius [?] was governing Syria.
Everyone went to be registered, each to his own town.
Joseph also went up from Galilee, from the town of Nazareth, to Judea, to the city of David called Bethlehem, because he belonged to the house and family of David,
to be registered with Mary, his betrothed wife, who was pregnant.
While they were there, the time came for her to give birth.
She bore her firstborn son, wrapped him in swaddling cloths, and laid him in a manger, because there was no room for them in the lodging place.
There were shepherds in that same region, staying awake and keeping watch over their flock at night.
And behold, an angel of the Lord stood among them, and the glory of the Lord shone around them, and they were very afraid.
The angel said to them, “Do not be afraid, for behold, I bring you good news of great joy, which will be for all the people:
Today a Savior has been born to you in the city of David, who is Christ the Lord.”
And this will be a sign for you: you will find a baby wrapped in swaddling cloths and lying in a manger.
And suddenly there was with the angel a multitude of the heavenly host, praising God and saying,
“Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, goodwill among people.”

And when the angels had gone away from them into heaven, the men, the shepherds, said to one another, “Let us go to Bethlehem and see this thing that has happened, which the Lord has made known to us.”
And they hurried there and found Mary and Joseph, and the baby lying in a manger.
When they saw him, they made known what had been said to them about this child.
And all who heard it were amazed at what the shepherds told them.
But Mary kept all these words in her heart.
And the shepherds returned, glorifying and praising God for everything they had heard and seen, just as it had been told to them.
And when eight days had passed and it was time to circumcise him, he was given the name Jesus, the name given by the angel before he was conceived in the womb.
They brought the child Jesus up to Jerusalem to present him before the Lord.
As it is written in the law of the Lord, “Every male child who first opens the womb shall be called holy to the Lord.”
And to offer a sacrifice according to what is said in the law of Moses: two turtledoves or two young pigeons.
And there was a man in Jerusalem whose name was Simeon. This man was righteous and devout, waiting for the consolation of Israel, and the Holy Spirit was in him.
And it had been revealed to him by the Holy Spirit that he would not see death before he saw the Lord’s Christ.
And he came into the temple in the Spirit. And when the parents brought in the child Jesus to do for him what was customary under the law,
he took him into his arms, and Simeon blessed God and said,
“Now, Master, you are letting your servant depart in peace, according to your word,
for my eyes have seen your salvation,
which you have prepared in the sight of all your peoples,
a light for revelation to the Gentiles and glory for your people Israel.”
And his father and mother were amazed at what was being said about him.
And Simeon blessed them and said to Mary his mother, “Look, this child is appointed for the fall and rising of many in Israel, and as a sign that will be opposed.
And a sword will pierce your own soul too, so that the thoughts of many hearts may be revealed.”
And there was a prophetess, Anna, the daughter of Phanuel, of the tribe of Asher. She was very advanced in years, having lived with her husband for seven years after her virginity.
She was a widow, eighty-[?] years old. She never left the temple, serving the Lord with fasting and prayers day and night.
She came up at that very hour and gave thanks to the Lord, and spoke about him to all who were waiting for deliverance in Jerusalem.
When they had completed everything according to the Lord’s law, they returned to Galilee, to their own town of Nazareth.
The child grew and became strong in spirit, being filled with wisdom, and the grace of God was upon him.
And his parents went to Jerusalem every year for the feast of Passover.
When he was twelve years old, they went up to Jerusalem according to the custom of the festival.
When the days were over and they were returning, the boy stayed behind in Jerusalem, and his parents did not know it.
Thinking that he was in the traveling company, they went a day’s journey and looked for him among their relatives and acquaintances.
When they did not find him, they returned to Jerusalem, searching for him.
After three days they found him in the temple, sitting among the teachers, listening to them and asking them questions.
All who heard him were amazed at his understanding and his answers.
When they saw him, they were astonished. His mother said to him, “Child, why have you treated us this way? Look, your father and I have been searching for you in distress.”
He said to them, “Why were you searching for me? Did you not know that I must be occupied with my Father’s affairs?”
But they did not understand what he said to them.
And he went down with them and came to Nazareth, and he was obedient to them. And his mother kept all these words in her heart.
And Jesus grew in wisdom and in stature, and in favor with God and people.

In the fifteenth year of the reign of Tiberius Caesar, when Pontius Pilate governed Judea, Herod was tetrarch of Galilee, his brother Philip was tetrarch of Iturea and the region of Trachonitis, and Lysanias was tetrarch of Abilene,
during the high priesthood of Annas and Caiaphas, the word of God came to John, the son of Zechariah, in the wilderness.
And he came into all the region around the Jordan, proclaiming baptism for the forgiveness of sins.
As it is written in the book of the words of Isaiah the prophet, who says: “The voice of one crying in the wilderness: Prepare the Lord’s way; make his paths straight.
Every valley will be filled, and every mountain and hill will be brought low. Crooked places will become straight, and rough places will become smooth paths.
And all flesh will see God’s salvation.”
He said to the crowds coming out to be baptized by him, “You brood of vipers! Who warned you to flee from the coming wrath?
Bear fruit worthy of repentance, and do not begin to say to yourselves, ‘We have Abraham as our father.’ For I tell you that God can raise up children for Abraham from these stones.
Already the axe lies at the root of the trees. Every tree that does not bear good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire.
The crowds asked him, saying, “Teacher, what should we do?”
He answered them, “Whoever has two tunics should give one to someone who has none, and whoever has food should do the same.”
Tax collectors also came to be baptized and said to him, “Teacher, what should we do?”
He said, “Do nothing beyond what you have been instructed.”
Soldiers also asked him, saying, “And what should we do?” He said to them, “Do not mistreat anyone or accuse anyone falsely, and be content with your pay.”
The people were waiting expectantly, and all were wondering in their hearts about John, whether he might be the Christ.

John answered them all, saying, “I baptize you with water, but someone more powerful than I is coming. I am not worthy to untie the strap of his sandals. He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and fire.
His winnowing shovel is in his hand, and he will clear his threshing floor and gather the wheat into his barn, but he will burn the chaff with unquenchable fire.”
And with many other words of encouragement he proclaimed the good news to the people.
Jesus came to Nazareth, where he had been brought up. As was his custom, he entered the synagogue on the Sabbath day and stood up to read.
They gave him the scroll of the prophet Isaiah. He unrolled the scroll and found the place where it was written:

“The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he has anointed me. He has sent me to proclaim good news to the poor, to heal the brokenhearted, to proclaim release to captives and recovery of sight to the blind, to set the oppressed free,
to proclaim the year of the Lord’s favor.”
He rolled up the scroll, gave it back to the attendant, and sat down. The eyes of everyone in the synagogue were fixed on him.
He began to say to them, “Today this scripture has been fulfilled in your hearing.”
And everyone spoke well of him and marveled at the words and grace that came from his mouth.
He said to them, “You will certainly tell me this proverb: ‘Physician, heal yourself.’” And they said to him, “Do here in your hometown all the things we have heard happened in Capernaum.”
He said, “Truly I tell you, no prophet is welcome in his hometown.
But I tell you the truth: there were many widows in Israel in the days of Elijah, when the sky was shut for three years and six months, and there was a great famine throughout the land.
Yet Elijah was sent to none of them, but only to a widow in Zarephath in the region of Sidon.
There were also many lepers in Israel in the time of Elisha the prophet, yet none of them was cleansed except Naaman the Assyrian.”
Everyone in the synagogues was filled with rage when they heard these things.
They rose up and drove him out of the town, and [?] him to the top of the hill on which their town was built, intending to throw him down.
But he passed through their midst and went on his way.
He entered Capernaum, a town in Galilee, and taught on the Sabbaths.
And they were astonished at his teaching, because his word had authority.
And in the synagogue there was a man who had an unclean demon. He cried out in a loud voice, saying,
“Leave us alone! What have you to do with us, Jesus of Nazareth? Have you come to destroy us? I know who you are—the Holy One of God.”
And Jesus rebuked him, saying, “Be silent and come out of him!” And the demon threw him down and came out of him without harming him at all.
And amazement came upon everyone, and they discussed it with one another, saying, “What is this word? For with authority and power he commands the unclean spirits, and they come out!”
Jesus was standing beside the Lake of Gennesaret.
And he saw two boats standing beside the lake, but the fishermen had left them and were washing their nets.
He got into one of the boats, which belonged to Simon, and asked him to put out a little from the shore. Then he sat down and taught the crowds from the boat.
When he had finished speaking, he said to Simon, “Put out into deep water, and let down your nets for a catch.”
And Simon answered him, “Master, we worked hard all night and caught nothing. But at your word we will let down the nets.”
And when they had done this, they caught a great number of fish, and their nets began to tear.
And they signaled to their partners in the other boat to come and help them. They came and filled both boats, so that they began to sink.
When Simon Peter saw this, he fell at Jesus’ knees, saying, “Go away from me, Lord, for I am a sinful man.”
For amazement had seized him and everyone with him at the catch of fish they had taken,
and likewise James and John, the sons of Zebedee, who were Simon’s partners. And Jesus said to [?], “Do not be afraid. From now on you will be catching people.”
And they brought the boat ashore, left everything, and followed him.
Jesus was teaching, and Pharisees and teachers of the law were sitting there. They had come from every village of Galilee and Judea and from Jerusalem. And the Lord’s power was present to heal them.
And there were men carrying on a bed a man who was paralyzed. They were trying to bring him in and lay him before Jesus.
But finding no way to bring him in because of the crowd, they went up onto the roof and lowered him with his bed through the tiles into
the middle, in front of Jesus. And when he saw their faith, he said, “Man, your sins are forgiven you.”
And the scribes and Pharisees began to reason, saying, “Who is this who speaks blasphemy? Who can forgive sins except God alone?”
But Jesus, knowing their thoughts, answered them, “What are you thinking in your hearts?”
Which is easier: to say to the paralyzed man, ‘Your sins are forgiven you,’ or to say, ‘Get up and walk’?
But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins”—he said to the paralyzed man—“I tell you, get up, pick up your bed, and go home.”
And immediately he stood up before them, picked up what he had been lying on, and went home, glorifying God.
And amazement seized everyone, and they glorified God and were filled with fear, saying, “We have seen wonderful things today.”
Jesus went out and saw a tax collector named Levi sitting at the tax booth. He said to him, “Follow me.”
And leaving everything, he got up and followed him.
Levi gave a great feast for him in his own house. There was a large crowd of tax collectors and others reclining at the table with them.
The scribes and Pharisees grumbled to his disciples, saying, “Why does he eat and drink with tax collectors and sinners?”
Jesus answered them, “Healthy people do not need a doctor, but sick people do.
I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.
Jesus was walking through grainfields on the Sabbath. His disciples were plucking heads of grain and eating them, rubbing them in their hands.
Some of the Pharisees said to them, “Why are you doing what is not lawful to do on the Sabbath?”
Jesus answered, “Have you not read what David did when he and those with him were hungry?”
how he [?] into the house of God, took the bread of the Presence and ate it, and also gave some to those with him? It was not lawful for anyone but the priests alone to eat it.”
And he said to them, “The Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath.”
On another Sabbath, he entered the synagogue and taught. A man was there whose right hand was withered.
The scribes watched him to see whether he would heal him on the Sabbath, so that they could find an accusation against him.
But he knew their thoughts and said to the man with the withered hand, “Get up and stand in the middle.” He got up and stood there.
Jesus said to them, “I ask you: Is it lawful on the Sabbath to do good or to do evil, to save a life or to destroy it?”
After looking around at them all, he said to him, “Stretch out your hand.” He stretched it out, and his hand was restored, as healthy as the other.
Crowds of Jesus’ disciples arrived, along with a great multitude of people from all Judea, Jerusalem, and the coastal region of Tyre and Sidon.
They came to hear him and to be healed of their diseases. Those suffering from their diseases were healed.
The whole crowd tried to touch him, because power was going out from him and healing them all.
He lifted his eyes toward his disciples and said, “Blessed are the poor in spirit, for yours is the kingdom of heaven.
Blessed are those who hunger now, for they will be filled. Blessed are those who weep now, for you will laugh.
Blessed will you be when people hate you, when they exclude you and reject your name as evil because of the Son of Man.
Rejoice on that day and leap for joy. Look, your reward in heaven is great.
As you want people to do to you, do the same to them.”
And if you love those who love you, what credit is that to you? For even sinners love those who love them.
And if you do good to those who do good to you, what credit is that to you? For even sinners do the same.
And if you lend to those from whom you expect repayment, what credit is that to you? For even sinners lend to sinners to receive the same amount back.
But love your enemies, do good to them, and lend, expecting nothing in return. Your reward will be great, and you will be sons of the Most High, for he is kind to the ungrateful and the wicked.
Be merciful, just as your Father is merciful.
Jesus entered Capernaum.
A certain centurion had a servant who was seriously ill and dying, and who was dear to him.
When he heard about Jesus, he sent elders of the people to him, asking him to come and save his servant.
They came to Jesus and pleaded earnestly with him, saying, “He is worthy of whatever you grant him,
for he loves our nation, and he built the synagogue for us.”

Jesus went with them. While he was still going with them, not far from the house, the centurion sent another man to him, saying, “Lord, do not trouble yourself, for I am not worthy to have you come under my roof.
That is why I did not consider myself worthy to come to you. But say the word, and my servant will be healed.
For I too am a man placed under authority, and I have soldiers under me. I say to one, ‘Go,’ and he goes, and to another, ‘Come,’ and he comes, and to my servant, ‘Do this,’ and he does it.”
When Jesus heard this, he marveled at him, and turning around, [?] found such great faith.
When those who had been sent returned to the house, they found that the sick servant had recovered.
Jesus was going to a town called Nain, and his disciples and a large crowd were going with him.
As they approached the town gate, a dead man was being carried out, his mother’s only son. She was a widow, and a large crowd from the town was with her.
When the Lord saw her, he had compassion on her and said to her, “Do not weep.”
He went up and touched the bier, and those carrying it stopped. He said, “Young man, I say to you, get up!”
The dead man sat up and began to speak.
Fear seized them all, and they glorified God, saying, “A great prophet has arisen among us,” and, “The Lord God has visited his people.”
A certain Pharisee asked Jesus to eat with him. He entered the Pharisee’s house and reclined at the table.
And a woman in the town who was a sinner, seeing that he was reclining at the table in the Pharisee’s house, brought an alabaster jar of perfume.
Standing behind him at his feet, weeping, she began to wet his feet with her tears. She wiped them with the hair of her head, kissed his feet, and anointed them with perfume.
When the Pharisee who had invited him saw this, he said to himself, “If this man were a prophet, he would know who and what kind of woman is touching him—that she is a sinner.”
Jesus answered him, “Simon, I have something to say to you.” He said, “Teacher, say it.”
“A certain moneylender had two debtors. One owed five hundred denarii, and the other fifty.
When neither had anything to repay him with, he forgave them both. Which of them, then, will love him more?”
Simon answered, “I suppose it is the one whose larger debt he forgave.” He said to him, “You have judged correctly.”
Turning toward the woman, he said to Simon, “Do you see this woman? I entered your house, and you gave me no water for my feet. But she wet my feet with her tears and wiped them with her hair.
You gave me no kiss, but from the time I came in, this woman has not stopped kissing my feet.
You did not anoint my head with oil, but she anointed my feet with [?].
Therefore I tell you, her many sins are forgiven, because she loved much. But whoever is forgiven little loves less.”
He said to her, “Your sins are forgiven.”
Those reclining at the table with him began to say among themselves, “Who is this who even forgives sins?”
He said to the woman, “Your faith has saved you. Go in peace.”
A sower went out to sow his seed. As he sowed it, some fell beside the path and was trampled, and the birds of the sky ate it.
Some fell on rock, and after sprouting it withered because it had no moisture.
Some fell among thorns, and the thorns grew and choked it.
Some fell on good soil, and after sprouting it produced a hundredfold crop.
His disciples asked him, “What does this parable mean?”

He said to them, “To you it has been given to know the mysteries of the kingdom of God, but to the others they are given in parables, so that seeing they may not see, and may not understand with their hearts.
This is the meaning of the parable: the seed is the word of God.
Those beside the path are the people who hear the word. Then the devil comes and takes the word from their hearts, so that they may not believe and be saved.
Those on the rock are the people who receive the word with joy when they hear it. But they have no root. They believe for a time, but in a time of testing they fall away.
What fell among the thorns represents those who hear, but as they go on their way, they are choked by the worries of wealth and the pleasures of life, and their fruit does not ripen.

But what fell on the good soil represents those who hear the word with a good and noble heart, hold on to it, and bear fruit with perseverance. As he said this, he called out, “Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear.”
“No one lights a lamp and covers it with a vessel or puts it under a bed. Instead, people put it on a lampstand, so that those who enter may see the light.
For nothing is hidden that will not be revealed, nor is anything concealed that will not become known and come into the open.
So take care how you listen. For whoever has will be given more, but whoever does not have, even what he thinks he has will be taken away from him.”
His mother and brothers came to him, but they could not speak with him because of the crowd.
He was told, “Your mother and your brothers are standing outside, wanting to see you.”
He answered them, “My mother and my brothers are those who hear the word of God and keep it.”
Jesus got into a boat with his disciples and said to them, “Let us cross to the other side of the lake.” And they set out.
As they sailed, he fell asleep. A windstorm swept down onto the lake, and they were perishing and [?].
They came to him and woke him, saying, “Master, we are perishing!” He got up and rebuked the wind and the raging water. They subsided, and there was calm.
He said to them, “Where is your faith?” Frightened and amazed, they said to one another, “Who is this, then? He commands even the winds and the water, and they obey him.”
When Jesus stepped ashore in the land of the Gadarenes, a certain man from the city met him. He had had a demon for many years. He wore no clothing and lived not in a house but among the tombs.
When he saw Jesus, he cried out, fell down before him, and said in a loud voice, “What have you to do with me, Jesus, Son of the living God? I beg you, do not torment me!”

For he was commanding the unclean spirit to come out of the man. For many years it had seized him, and they bound him with iron chains and shackles and kept him under guard. But he would break the bonds and be driven by the demon through the wilderness.
Jesus asked him, “What is your name?” He said, “Legion,” because many demons had entered him.
They begged him not to command them to go into the abyss.
A large herd of pigs was feeding there on the hillside. They begged him to let them enter the pigs, and he allowed them.
The demons came out of the man and entered the pigs. The herd rushed down the steep bank into the lake and drowned.
When the herders saw what had happened, they fled and reported it in the city and in the villages.
People went out to see what had happened. They came to Jesus and found the man from whom the demons had come out sitting at Jesus’ feet, clothed and in his right mind. And they were afraid.
The man from whom the demons had come out begged to stay with him. But Jesus sent him away, saying,
“Return to your home and tell how much God has done for you.” He went throughout the whole city, telling how much Jesus had done for him.
A certain man named Jairus came to Jesus. He was a ruler of the synagogue. He fell at Jesus’ feet and begged him to come into his house,
because he had an only daughter, about twelve years old, and she was dying. As Jesus went, the crowds pressed around him.
And there was a woman who had suffered from bleeding for twelve years. She had spent all she had on physicians, but could not be healed by any of them.
She came up behind him and touched the hem of his garment. Immediately her bleeding stopped.
Jesus said, “Who touched me?” When everyone denied it, Peter and those with him said, “Master, the crowds are pressing and pushing against you, and you say, ‘Who touched me?’”
But Jesus said, “Someone touched me, for I felt power go out from me.”
When she saw that she had not escaped notice, she came trembling and fell down before him. In front of all the people, she told him why she had touched him and how she had been healed immediately.
Jesus said to her, “Take courage, daughter. Your faith has saved you. Go in peace.”
While he was still speaking, someone came from the synagogue and said to him, “Your daughter has died. Do not trouble the teacher.”
But when Jesus heard this, he answered him, “Do not be afraid. Only believe, and she will be saved.”
When he came to the house, he allowed no one to go in with him except Peter, John, James, and the girl’s father and mother.
Everyone was weeping and mourning for her. But he said, “Do not weep. The girl is not dead but asleep.”
They laughed at him, knowing that she had died.
But he sent everyone out, took her by the hand, and called to her, saying, “Girl, get up.”
Her spirit returned, and she rose at once. He ordered that she be given something to eat.
Her parents were astonished, but he commanded them to tell no one what had happened.
He called his twelve disciples together and gave them power and authority over all demons and to heal diseases.
He sent them to proclaim the kingdom of God and to heal the sick.
He said to them, “Take nothing for the journey: no staff, no bag, no bread, no money. Do not have two tunics.
Whatever house you enter, stay there, and leave from there.
Wherever people do not welcome you, shake the dust off your feet as you leave that town, as a testimony against them.”
They set out and went through the villages, proclaiming the good news and healing everywhere.
“Whoever wants to follow me must deny himself, take up his cross every day, and follow me.
For whoever wants to save his life will lose it, but whoever loses his life for my sake will save it.
What does a person gain if he acquires the whole world but destroys or forfeits himself?
For whoever is ashamed of me and my words, the Son of Man will also be ashamed of him when he comes in his own glory and the glory of the Father and the holy angels.
But I tell you truly, there are some standing here who will not taste death until they see the kingdom of God.”
When Jesus came down from the mountain, a large crowd met him.
A man from the crowd cried out, saying, “Teacher, I beg you, look at my son, because he is my only child.
A spirit seizes him, and he suddenly cries out and convulses, foaming at the mouth. It hardly ever leaves him, and it batters him.
I begged your disciples to drive it out, but they could not.”
Jesus answered, “O faithless and corrupt generation, how long must I remain among you and put up with you? Bring your son here to me.”
While he was still coming, the demon threw him down and shook him violently. But Jesus rebuked the unclean spirit, healed the boy, and gave him back to his mother.
Everyone was amazed at the greatness of God.
As Jesus was going along the road, someone said to him, “Lord, I will follow you wherever you go.”
Jesus said to him, “Foxes have dens, and the birds of the sky have nests, but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head.”
He said to another, “Follow me.” But he said, “Lord, first let me go and bury my father.”
Jesus said to him, “Leave the dead to bury their own dead. But you, go and proclaim the kingdom of God.”
Another said, “I will follow you, Lord, but first let me say goodbye to those in my household.”
Jesus said to him, “No one who puts his hand to the plow and looks back is fit for the kingdom of God.”
Jesus sent his disciples ahead of him in pairs to every town and place where he himself intended to go.
He said to them, “The harvest is plentiful, but the workers are few. So pray to the Lord of the harvest to send out workers into his harvest.
Go! Look, I am sending you out like sheep among wolves.
Whatever town you enter where they do not welcome you, go out into its streets and say,
‘Even the dust from this town that clings to our feet we shake off against you. Yet know this: the kingdom of God has come near to you.’
But I tell you, on that day it will be more bearable for Sodom than for that city.
“Whoever listens to you listens to me, and whoever listens to me listens to the one who sent me. Whoever rejects you rejects me, and whoever rejects me rejects the one who sent me.”
The seventy returned with joy, saying, “Lord, even the demons submit to us in your name.”
He said to them, “I saw Satan fall from heaven like lightning.
Look, I have given you authority to tread on snakes and scorpions and over all the power of the enemy, and nothing will harm you.
Yet do not rejoice that the spirits submit to you. Instead, rejoice that your names are written in heaven.”

At that moment Jesus rejoiced in spirit and said, “I praise you, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because you have hidden these things from the wise and understanding and revealed them to little children. Yes, Father, for this was pleasing to you.”

Turning to the disciples, he said, “All things have been handed over to me by my Father. No one knows who the Son is except the Father, or who the Father is except the Son and anyone to whom the Son chooses to reveal him.”
Turning to the disciples, he said privately, “Blessed are the eyes that see what you see.
For I tell you that many prophets and kings wanted to see what you see but did not see it, and to hear what you hear but did not hear it.”
An expert in the law came to Jesus to test him, saying, “Teacher, what must I do to inherit eternal life?”
He said to him, “What is written in the Law? How do you read it?”
He answered, “You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your strength, and with all your mind love him, and your neighbor as yourself.”
Jesus said to him, “You have answered correctly. Do this, and you will live.”
But he, wanting to justify himself, said to Jesus, “And who is my neighbor?”
Jesus answered and said, “A man was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho and fell among robbers. They stripped him, wounded him, and went away, leaving him barely alive.”
By chance a priest was going down that road, and when he saw him, he passed by.
Likewise a Levite came to the same place, and when he came up and saw him, he passed by.
But a Samaritan who was traveling came upon him, and when he saw him, he had compassion on him.
He went up to him and bandaged his wounds, pouring on oil and wine. Then he put him on his own animal, brought him to an inn, and cared for him.
The next day, as he was leaving, he took out two denarii and gave them to the innkeeper, saying, ‘Take care of him, and whatever more you spend, I will repay you when I return.’
Which of these three do you think was a neighbor to the man who fell among the robbers?”
He said, “The one who showed him mercy.” Jesus said to him, “Go and do likewise.”
Jesus entered a village, and a woman named Martha welcomed him into her home.
She had a sister called Mary, who sat at Jesus’ feet and listened to his word.
But Martha was distracted by much serving. She came up and said, “Lord, do you not care that my sister has left me to serve you alone? Tell her to help me.”
Jesus answered and said to her, “Martha, Martha, you are worried and troubled about many things.”
But one thing is needed. Mary has chosen the good portion, which will not be taken away from her.”
“Which of you has a friend and goes to him at midnight and says to him, ‘Friend, lend me three loaves of bread’?”
because a friend of mine has come to me from a journey, and I have nothing to set before him’?
And the one inside answers, ‘Do not trouble me. The door is already shut, and my children are with me in bed. I cannot get up and give you anything.’
I tell you, even if he will not get up and give him anything because he is his friend, yet because of his shameless persistence he will get up and give him as much as he needs.
And I tell you: ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and it will be opened to you.
For everyone who asks receives, and the one who seeks finds, and to the one who knocks it will be opened.
Which father among you, if his son asks him for bread, will give him a stone? Or if he asks for a fish, will he give him a snake instead of a fish?
Or if he asks for an egg, will he give him a scorpion?
“If you, then, who are evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your heavenly Father give a good spirit to those who ask him!”
While he was saying these things, a woman in the crowd raised her voice and said to him, “Blessed is the womb that carried you, and the breasts that you nursed at!”
But he said, “Rather, blessed are those who hear the word of God and keep it.”
Nothing is covered that will not be uncovered, or hidden that will not become known.
For whatever you have said in the dark will be heard in the light, and what you have whispered into someone’s ear in private rooms will be proclaimed on the rooftops.
I tell you, my friends, do not be afraid of those who kill the body and after that can do nothing more.
But I will show you whom you should fear: fear the one who, after killing, has authority to throw you into Gehenna. Yes, I tell you, fear him.
Are not five sparrows sold for two small coins? Yet not one of them is forgotten before God.
Even the hairs of your head are all counted. So do not be afraid; you are worth more than many sparrows.
I tell you, everyone who acknowledges me before people, I will also acknowledge before the angels of God.
But whoever denies me before people will be denied before the angels of God.
Everyone who speaks a word against the Son of Man will be forgiven, but whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven.
When they bring you before synagogues, authorities, and rulers, do not worry about how or what you should think, or what you should say.
“For the Holy Spirit will teach you at that moment what you should say.”
The Lord told this parable: “A certain man’s field produced abundantly.
He thought to himself, saying, ‘What shall I do? I have nowhere to gather my crops.’
Then he said, ‘This is what I will do: I will tear down my barn and build a larger one, and there I will gather all my grain and my goods.
And I will say to my soul, “Soul, you have many good things stored up for many years. Rest, eat, drink, and be merry.”’
But God said to him, ‘Fool! This very night your soul will be demanded of you. And the things you have prepared—whose will they be?’
“So it is with everyone who stores up treasure for himself but is not rich toward God.” After saying this, he called out, “Let anyone who has ears to hear listen!”
Do not be afraid, little flock, for your Father has been pleased to give you the kingdom.
Sell your possessions and give to the poor. Make yourselves money bags that do not wear out, an unfailing treasure in heaven, where no thief comes near and no moth destroys.
For where your treasure is, there your hearts will also be.
Keep your waists belted and your lamps burning.
Be like people waiting for their master to return from a wedding, so that when he comes and knocks, they can open the door for him at once.
And blessed are those servants whom the master finds keeping watch. Truly I tell you, he will fasten his belt, have them sit down at the table, and come and serve them.
Whether he comes in the second watch or the third watch and finds them ready like this, blessed are those servants.
But know this: if the owner of the house had known at what hour the thief would come, he would have kept watch and would not have allowed his house to be broken into.
“You too must be ready, because the Son of Man will come at an hour when you do not expect him.”
Jesus was teaching in one of the synagogues on the Sabbath.
And there was a woman who had had a spirit of infirmity for sixteen years. She was bent over and could not straighten up at all.
When Jesus saw her, he called her over and said to her, “Woman, you are freed from your illness.”
He laid his hands on her, and immediately she straightened up and glorified God.

But the ruler of the synagogue, indignant because Jesus had healed her on the Sabbath, said to the crowd, “There are six days on which work should be done. Come on those days and be healed, and not on the Sabbath day.”
The Lord answered him and said, “Hypocrites! Does not each of you untie his ox or donkey from the manger on the Sabbath and lead it away to give it water?”
“And should not this woman, a daughter of Abraham whom Satan has bound for eighteen years now, be freed from this bond on the Sabbath day?”
As he said these things, all his opponents were put to shame, and all the people rejoiced at all the glorious things being done by him.
The kingdom of heaven is like a mustard seed that a man took and planted in his garden. It grew and became a large tree, and the birds of the sky made their homes in its branches.
And again he said, “To what shall I compare the kingdom of God?
It is like leaven that a woman took and hid in three measures of flour until all of it was leavened.”
He went through towns and villages, teaching as he made his way toward Jerusalem.
Someone said to him, “Lord, are only a few being saved?” And he said to him,
“Strive to enter through the narrow gate, because many, I tell you, will seek to enter and will not be able.

“Once the master of the house gets up and shuts the door, you will begin to stand outside and knock at the door, saying, ‘Lord, Lord, open for us!’ But he will answer you, ‘I do not know you or where you come from.’”
Then you will begin to say, ‘We ate and drank in your presence, and you taught us in our streets.’
“And he will say, ‘I tell you, I do not know you or where you come from. Depart from me, all you who do evil!’”
There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth when you see Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and all the prophets in the kingdom of God, but you yourselves thrown out.
People will come from east and west, north and south, and sit down at the table in the kingdom of God. ✝
Jesus entered the house of one of the leaders of the Pharisees on the Sabbath to eat bread, and they were watching him closely.
And there before him was a man suffering from dropsy.
Jesus answered the experts in the law and the Pharisees, saying, “Is it lawful to heal him on the Sabbath?”
But they remained silent. He took hold of him, healed him, and sent him away.
Then he answered, “Which of you, if his donkey or ox falls into a well, will not immediately pull it out on the Sabbath day?”
And they could not answer him.
He told a parable to those who had been invited, noticing how they chose the places of honor. He said to them:
“When someone invites you to a wedding feast, do not sit in the place of honor, lest someone more distinguished than you be among those invited.
Then the one who invited you and him will come and say to you, ‘Give this man your place,’ and you will begin, in shame, to take the lowest place.

But when you are invited, go and sit in the lowest place, so that when the one who invited you comes, he will say to you, ‘Friend, move up higher.’ Then you will be honored before all those sitting at the table with you.
“For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.”
A certain man prepared a great dinner and invited many people.
At the time for dinner, he sent his servant to tell those who had been invited, ‘Come, for everything is now ready.’
But they all alike began to make excuses. The first said to him, ‘I have bought a field, and I need to go out and see it. Please excuse me.’
Another said to him, ‘I have bought five yoke of oxen, and I am going to try them out. Please excuse me.’
Another said, ‘I have married a wife, and therefore I cannot come.’

The servant returned and reported these things to his master. Then the master of the house became angry and said to his servant, ‘Go out quickly into the streets and squares of the city, and bring the poor, the disabled, the lame, and the blind in here.’
The servant said to his master, ‘What you commanded has been done, and there is still room.’
Then the master said to the servant, ‘Go out to the roads and hedges and urge people to come in, so that my house may be filled.
“For I tell you that not one of those men who were invited will taste my supper. For many are called, but few are chosen.”
A certain man had two sons.
The younger son said to his father, “Father, give me the share of the property that belongs to me.” And he divided his property between them.
Not many days later, the younger son gathered everything together and went away to a distant country. There he squandered his property in reckless living.
When he had spent everything, a severe famine arose in that country, and he began to be in need.
He went and attached himself to one of the citizens of that country, who sent him into his fields to tend pigs.
He longed to fill himself with the pods that the pigs were eating, but no one gave him anything.
When he came to his senses, he said, ‘How many of my father’s hired servants have more than enough bread, while I am perishing here from hunger!’
I will get up and go to my father and say to him, ‘Father, I have sinned against heaven and before you.’
‘I am no longer worthy to be called your son. Make me like one of your hired workers.’
And he got up and went to his father. While he was still not far away, his father saw him and felt compassion for him. He ran, threw his arms around his neck, and kissed him.
The son said to him, “Father, I have sinned against heaven and before you. I am no longer worthy to be called your son. Make me like one of your hired workers.”
But his father said to his servants, ‘Quickly, bring out the best robe and dress him in it. Put a ring on his hand and sandals on his feet.’
‘And bring the fattened calf and slaughter it. Let us eat and celebrate.’
‘For this son of mine was dead and has come back to life. He was lost, and [?] and was found.’ And they began to celebrate.
Now his older son was in the field. As he came and drew near the house, he heard music and dancing.
He called one of the servants and asked him what these things meant.
The servant said to him, ‘Your brother has come, and your father has slaughtered the fattened calf because he has received him back safe and sound.’
But he became angry and would not go in. His father came out and pleaded with him.
But he answered his father, ‘Look, all these years I have served you and have never disobeyed your command. Yet you have never given me even a young goat so that I could celebrate with my friends.’
‘But when this son of yours came, after squandering your property with prostitutes, you slaughtered the fattened calf for him.’
He said to him, ‘Child, you are always with me, and everything I have is yours.’
“But it was right to celebrate and rejoice, because this brother of yours was dead and has come to life; he was lost and has been found.”
Whoever is faithful in very little is also faithful in much, and whoever is dishonest in very little is also dishonest in much.
So if you have not been faithful with unrighteous wealth, who will entrust you with true wealth?
And if you have not been faithful with what belongs to someone else, who will give you what is your own?
For no servant can serve two masters: either he will hate one and love the other, or he will hold fast to one and begin to neglect the other. You cannot serve God and wealth.
The Pharisees, who were lovers of money, heard all these things and mocked him.
And he said to them, “You are the ones who justify yourselves before people, but God knows your hearts. For what is highly valued among people is an abomination before God.”
There was a certain rich man who dressed in purple and fine linen and lived in splendid enjoyment every day.
There was also a certain poor man named Lazarus, who lay at his gates, covered with sores.
He longed to fill himself with the crumbs that fell from the rich man’s table. Even the dogs came and licked his sores.
The poor man died and was carried by angels to Abraham’s bosom. The rich man also died and was buried, and in Hades.
And being in torment, he raised his eyes and saw Abraham far away, and Lazarus at his side.
And he cried out, saying, “Father Abraham, have mercy on me, and send Lazarus to dip the tip of his finger in water and cool my tongue, for I am suffering in this flame.”
But Abraham said to him, “Child, remember that you received your good things during your lifetime, and Lazarus likewise received bad things. But now he is comforted here, while you suffer.”
“And besides all this, a great chasm has been established between you and us, so that those who want to cross cannot, nor can those from there cross over to us.”
Then he said, “I beg you, then, father, to send him to my father’s house.”
“For I have five brothers. Let him warn them, so that they too do not come to this place of torment.”
But Abraham said, “They have Moses and the prophets. Let them listen to them.”
But he said, “No, Father Abraham, but if someone from the dead goes to them, they will repent.”
He said to him, “If they do not listen to Moses and the prophets, they will not believe even if someone rises from the dead.”
“Watch yourselves. If your brother sins, rebuke him, and if he repents, forgive him.”
“And if he sins against you seven times in a day, and seven times turns back to you, saying, ‘I repent,’ forgive him.”
And the apostles said to the Lord, “Increase our faith.”
And the Lord said, “If you had faith like a mustard seed, you could say to this mulberry tree, ‘Be uprooted and planted in the sea,’ and it would obey you.”
“Which of you, having a servant plowing or tending a flock, will say to him when he comes in from the field, ‘Come at once and recline at the table’?”
“Will he not instead say to him, ‘Prepare something for my supper, fasten your belt, and serve me while I eat and drink? Afterward you may eat and drink.’”
“Does he thank that servant because he did what he was commanded? I think not.”
So you too, when you have done what you were commanded, say, “We are unworthy servants. We have done what we were obliged to do.”
As Jesus was entering a certain village, ten men with leprosy met him. They stood at a distance.
And they raised their voices, saying, “Jesus, Master, have mercy on us!”
And when he saw them, he said to them, “Go and show yourselves to the priests.” And as they went, they were cleansed.
But one of them, seeing that he had been healed, returned, glorifying God with a loud voice.
And he fell face down at his knees, giving him thanks. And he was a Samaritan.
Jesus answered, “Were not ten cleansed? But the nine [?]”
“How is it that none were found returning to give glory to God except this foreigner?”
And he said to him, “Get up and go. Your faith has saved you.”
There was a judge in a certain city who neither feared God nor respected anyone.
There was a widow in that city, and she kept coming to him, saying, “Give me justice against my opponent.”
For a long time he refused, but afterward he said to himself, “Though I neither fear God nor respect anyone,
because this widow keeps troubling me, I will give her justice, so that she does not wear me out by continually coming.”
The Lord said, “Listen to what the unjust judge says.
And will not God bring justice for his chosen ones, who cry out to him day and night, though he is patient with them?
I tell you that he will quickly bring justice for them.
Two men went up to the temple to pray, one a Pharisee and the other a tax collector.
The Pharisee stood and prayed to himself like this: “God, I thank you that I am not like other people—robbers, wrongdoers, adulterers—or like this tax collector.
I fast twice a week and give a tenth of everything I acquire.”
But the tax collector stood far off and would not even lift his eyes to heaven. Instead, he beat his chest, saying, “God, be merciful to me, a sinner.”
I tell you, this man went down to his home justified rather than the other. For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.
A certain man came to Jesus, testing him and saying, “Good teacher, what must I do to inherit eternal life?”
Jesus said to him, “Why do you call me good? No one is good except God alone.
You know the commandments: Do not murder. Do not commit adultery. Do not steal. Do not bear false witness. Honor your father and your mother.”
He said to him, “I have kept all these from my youth.”
When Jesus heard this, he said to him, “You still lack one thing. Sell everything you have and distribute it to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven. Then come, follow me.”
When he heard this, he became deeply saddened, for he was very rich.
When Jesus saw that he was deeply saddened, he said, “How hard it is for those who have wealth to enter the kingdom of God!
For it is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle than for a rich person to enter the kingdom of God.”
Those who heard this said, “Who can be saved?”
But he said, “What is impossible for human beings is all possible for God.”
As Jesus approached Jericho, a certain blind man was sitting beside the road begging.
When he heard a crowd passing by, he asked what was happening.
They told him that Jesus of Nazareth was passing by.
And he cried out, saying, “Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!”
Those walking ahead rebuked him, telling him to be quiet. But he cried out all the more, saying, “Son of David, have mercy!”
Jesus stopped and ordered him to be brought to him. When he came near, Jesus asked him,
“What do you want me to do for you?” He said, “Lord, let me see again.”
Jesus said to him, “Receive your sight. Your faith has saved you.”
And immediately he regained his sight and followed him, glorifying God. And all the people, when they saw it, gave praise to God.
Jesus entered Jericho.
And there was a man named Zacchaeus. He was a chief tax collector, and he was rich.
He was trying to see who Jesus was, but he could not because of the crowd, since he was short.
So he ran ahead and climbed a sycamore tree to see Jesus, because he was about to pass that way.
When Jesus came to the place, he looked up, saw him, and said to him, “Zacchaeus, hurry and come down, for today I must stay at your house.”
He hurried down and welcomed him joyfully.
When they saw him, they grumbled, saying, “He has gone in to stay with a sinful man.”
Zacchaeus stood and said to the Lord, “Look, Lord, I will give half of my possessions to the poor. And if I have defrauded anyone of anything, I will repay it sevenfold.”
Jesus said to him, “Today salvation has come to this house, because he too is a son of Abraham.
For the Son of Man came to seek and save the one who was lost.
A man of noble birth went to a distant country to receive a kingdom and then return.
He called ten of his servants, gave them ten minas, and said to them, “Trade with these until I return.”
But his citizens did not want him, and they sent a petition after him, saying, “We do not want this man to reign over us.”
When he returned, having received the kingdom, he ordered the servants to whom he had given the money to be summoned to him, so that he could find out what they had earned by trading.
The first came and said, “Master, your mina has earned ten minas.”
He said to him, “Good and faithful servant! Because you have been faithful in a small matter, have authority over ten cities.”
The second came and said, “Master, your mina has made five minas.”
He said to him also, “You too shall be over five cities.”
Another came and said, “Master, here is your mina, which I kept wrapped in a cloth.
For I was afraid of you, because you are a harsh man. You take up what you did not put down and reap where you did not sow.
And he said to him, “By your own words I judge you, wicked servant. You knew that I am a harsh man, taking what I did not put down and reaping what I did not sow.”
Why, then, did you not give my money to the bankers? When I returned, I could have collected it with interest.”
And he said to those standing nearby, “Take the mina from him and give it to the one who has ten minas.”

But I tell you that everyone who has will be given more, while from the one who does not have, even what he has will be taken away. Having said this, he called out, “Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear.”
The Lord said to his disciples:
“Beware of the scribes, who like to walk around in robes and love greetings in the marketplaces, the foremost seats in the synagogues, and the places of honor at dinners.
They devour widows’ houses and make long prayers for show. They will receive greater condemnation.”
Looking up, he saw rich people putting their gifts into the treasury.
He also saw a certain poor widow putting two small coins into it.
And he said, “Truly I tell you, this poor widow has put in more than all the others.

For all these people contributed to the offerings out of their abundance, but she, out of her poverty, put in her entire livelihood, all that she had. Having said these things, he called out, “Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear.”
The Lord said, “Be watchful. Do not be terrified, for many will come in my name, saying, ‘I am he,’ and ‘My time has drawn near.’ Do not follow them.
When you hear of wars and disturbances, do not be afraid. These things must happen first, but the end will not come immediately.
For they will lay their hands on you and persecute you, handing you over to synagogues and prisons. You will be brought before kings and rulers for my name’s sake.
This will give you an opportunity to bear witness.
Therefore settle it in your hearts not to prepare your defense beforehand.
For I will give you words and wisdom that none of your opponents will be able to resist or answer.
You will be betrayed by parents, brothers, relatives, and friends, and they will put some of you to death.
And you will be hated by everyone for my name’s sake.
But not a hair of your head will perish.
Through your endurance, gain your souls.
“And there will be signs in the sun, moon, and stars, and on earth distress among the nations, in despair at the roaring and turmoil of the sea.
People will faint from fear and anticipation of what is coming upon the world, for the powers of heaven will be shaken.
And then you will see the Son of Man coming on the clouds with power and great glory.
Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away.
But watch yourselves, lest your hearts be weighed down with overeating, drunkenness, and the worries of life, and that day come upon you suddenly.
For it will come like a trap upon all who live on the face of the whole earth.
Therefore, stay awake at all times, praying that you may be found worthy to escape all these things that are about to happen and to stand before the Son of Man.
An angel from heaven appeared to him, strengthening him.
And being in agony, he prayed more earnestly, and his sweat became like drops of blood falling to the ground.
And rising from prayer,
Two other criminals [?] with Jesus, to be put to death.
And when they came to the place called the Skull, there they crucified him and both criminals, one on his right and the other on his left.
But Jesus said, “Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they are doing.” And they cast lots as they divided his garments.
The people stood watching. The rulers also mocked him along with them, saying, “He saved others; let him save himself, if he is the Christ, the Son of God, the Chosen One.”
The soldiers also mocked him, coming up and offering him vinegar,
and saying, “If you are the King of the Jews, save yourself.”
There was also an inscription written above him in Greek, Latin, and Hebrew letters: “This is the King of the Jews.”
One of the criminals who were hanging there reviled him, saying, “If you are the Christ, save yourself and us.”
But the other answered and rebuked him, saying, “Do you not fear God, since you are under the same sentence?
And we are condemned justly, for we are receiving what we deserve for what we have done. But this man has done nothing wrong.”
And he said to Jesus, “Remember me, Lord, when you come into your kingdom.”
And Jesus said to him, “Truly I tell you, today you will be with me in paradise.”
It was about the sixth hour, and darkness came over the whole land until the ninth hour.
The sun grew dark, and the curtain of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom.
And Jesus cried out with a loud voice and said, “Father, into your hands I entrust my spirit.” And after saying this, he breathed his last.
When the centurion saw what had happened, he glorified God, saying, “Truly this man was righteous.”
And all who had come to this spectacle, seeing what was happening, went back beating their breasts.
And all who knew him stood at a distance, along with the women who had come with him from Galilee, watching these things.
On the first day of the week, very early in the morning, the women came to the tomb, bringing the spices they had prepared, and some other women came with them.
They found the stone rolled away from the tomb.
But when they went in, they did not find the body of the Lord Jesus there.
While they were puzzled about this, suddenly two men stood beside them in shining clothes.
The women were terrified and bowed their faces to the ground. The men said to them, “Why do you seek the living among the dead?
He is not here, but has risen. Remember how he spoke to you while he was still in Galilee,
saying that the Son of Man must be handed over into the hands of sinful men, be crucified, and rise again on the third day.”
And they remembered his words.
Returning from the tomb, they reported all these things to the eleven and to all the others.
It was Mary Magdalene, Joanna, Mary the mother of James, and the other women with them who told these things to the apostles.
But their words seemed like nonsense to them, and they did not believe the women.
But Peter got up and ran to the tomb. Stooping down, he saw only the linen cloths lying there, and he went away, wondering to himself at what had happened.
Now that same day, two of them were going to a village called Emmaus, sixty stadia from Jerusalem.
They were talking with each other about all these things that had happened.
While they were talking and discussing these things, Jesus himself came near and walked with them.
But their eyes were kept from recognizing him.
He said to them, “What are these things you are discussing with each other as you walk, and why are you sad?”
One of them, named Cleopas, answered him, “Are you the only visitor to Jerusalem who does not know what has happened there in these days?”
He said to them, “What things?” They said to him, “The things concerning Jesus of Nazareth, who was a prophet mighty in deed and word before God and all the people,
and how our chief priests and rulers handed him over to be condemned to death and crucified him.
But we had hoped that he was the one who would redeem Israel. Besides all this, today is the third day since these things happened.
Some women from our group also astonished us. They went to the tomb early in the morning,
and when they did not find his body, they came back saying that they had also seen a vision of an angel, who said that he was alive.
Some of those with us went to the tomb and found it just as the women had said, but they did not see him.”
And he said to the two of them, “How foolish you are, and slow of heart to believe all that the prophets have spoken!”
Was it not necessary for Christ to suffer these things, rise from the dead, and enter into his glory?
And beginning with Moses and all the prophets, he explained to them the Scriptures that had been written about him.
They approached the village to which they were going, and he acted as though he would go farther.
They urged him, saying, “Stay with us, because it is nearly evening, and the day is already drawing to a close.” And he went in to stay with them.
And when he reclined at the table with them, he took bread, blessed it, broke it, and gave it to them.
Their eyes were opened, and they recognized him, and he vanished from their sight.
And they said to each other, “Was not our heart burning within us when he spoke to us on the road and explained the Scriptures to us?”
And they rose that very hour and returned to Jerusalem. They found the eleven gathered together, along with those who were with them,
saying, “He has truly risen [?] and has appeared to Simon.”
And the two of them told what had happened on the road and how he had become known to them in the breaking of the bread.
He stood among his disciples and said to them, “Peace be with you. It is I; do not be afraid.”
But they were frightened and terrified and thought they were seeing a spirit.
And he said to them, “Why are you troubled, and why do doubts arise in your hearts?
Look at my hands and my feet: it is I myself. Touch me and see, for a spirit does not have flesh and bones, as you see that I have.”
And after saying this, he showed them his hands, his feet, and his side.
While they still disbelieved because of their joy and were amazed, he said to them, “Do you have anything here to eat?”
They gave him a piece of roasted fish and some honeycomb.
And he ate in front of them and gave them what remained.
And he said to them, “These are the words that I spoke to you while I was still alive: everything written about me in the Law of Moses, the Prophets, and the Psalms must be fulfilled.”
Then he opened their minds so that they could understand the Scriptures.
And he said to them, “This is what is written, and thus it was necessary for Christ to suffer and rise from the dead on the third day,
and for repentance and forgiveness of sins to be proclaimed in his name among all nations, beginning from Jerusalem.
You are witnesses to these things.
And see, I will send the promise of my Father upon you. But remain in the city of Jerusalem until you are clothed with power from above.”
And he led them out as far as Bethany, and raising his hands, he blessed them.
And as he blessed them, he parted from them and was carried up into heaven.
And they worshiped him and returned to Jerusalem with great joy.
And they were continually in the temple, praising God and blessing the Lord. Amen.
